title: Functional programming: immutability, pure functions and side effects

videos.script: A function that charges a fine can give two different answers to the same question. {{title}} It reads a setting somebody else can change. It writes to a log. It asks the clock what day it is. Each of those is a side effect, and each makes the function harder to trust. {{effects}} Functional programming is a discipline for keeping them in their place. {{discipline}} A pure function depends only on its arguments, and does nothing except return a value. {{pure}} An immutable value cannot change behind your back, so a renewal makes a new loan instead of editing the old one. {{immutable}} The effects do not disappear. Somebody still has to send the e-mail. They move to a thin shell around a core of pure functions. {{shell}} Then come the tools that make pure code pleasant. Functions passed as values, pipelines, map, filter and reduce. {{tools}} And errors returned as values, so a bad line in a file is data to report, not a crash. {{errors}} None of this needs a functional language. Python, Java, Go and TypeScript all have it. {{languages}}
